details.label: Discussion
details.text: To the south/southeast of a low-amplitude digging short wave trough, latest Rapid Refresh output suggests that warm advection in the 850-700 mb layer will gradually become focused in corridor roughly east of Pierre SD into the Spencer IA vicinity through 08-09Z. Isolated intensifying thunderstorm development is already underway within this regime to the southwest of Sioux Falls, and a further increase during the next few hours appears possible, though this is not depicted particularly well by convection allowing guidance. Beneath steep mid-level lapse rates, inflow of moist air supportive of large CAPE on the order of 2000-3000+ J/kg may support elevated supercells capable of producing large hail, in the presence of strong cloud-bearing layer shear. This appears likely to be rooted above a relatively deep saturated surface-based layer with generally weak to stable lapse rates. So, while localized downbursts might still be possible, the potential for damaging surface gusts may be generally slow to evolve, and await substantive consolidation and upscale growth
